title: Organizing the Temple Musicians
overview: David organizes the families of three master musicians into 24 groups that take turns leading music in worship, with the order decided by drawing lots.

parts.label: Musicians set apart (vv. 1-3)
parts.note: David and his army leaders chose the sons of three master musicians, Asaph, Jeduthun and Heman, to lead worship with harps, lyres and cymbals. Their work is called "prophesying," which here seems to mean praise and thanks given under God's inspiration rather than predicting the future.

parts.label: Heman's large family (vv. 4-6)
parts.note: Heman is called the king's seer, meaning someone who passed on messages from God, and his fourteen sons and three daughters are presented as a gift that honored him. Many scholars notice that the later sons' names, read together in Hebrew, sound like a line of a prayer or psalm, though no one is sure why.

parts.label: Skilled and chosen by lot (vv. 7-8)
parts.note: There were 288 trained musicians, which makes 24 groups of twelve. They drew lots to set their order, so young and old, teacher and student, were treated alike instead of being ranked by age or status.

parts.label: The 24 rotations (vv. 9-31)
parts.note: Each group of twelve took its turn leading the music, probably for a week at a time, matching the 24 rotations of priests set up in the previous chapter. The order drawn mixes the three families and often puts younger sons ahead of older ones.

think: When a group decides who goes first, what is gained or lost by leaving it to chance instead of age, rank or skill?
